knowledge_point.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector in a Diagram

question.:question/problem:
![](/media/jake/SSD/EDB/math/images/9d/9dfaf74a497a2fd22428e09a4c26d573e184c9728ccf67f11ebb9d6a2a44f4c6.png)

Consider the picture above. Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $q + r$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we have to find $q+r$. According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $q+r$ goes from the tail of $q$ to the head of $r$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096814/assets/613ba59bf79f8566053088209dba7df73aa840a2e3bf19d6805f6b2b93254dce-solution.png)

In $\bigtriangleup AHB$ we have $\angle AHB=90^\circ$, $AH=4$ and $BH=1.5$. So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
AB &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\
&= \sqrt{(4)^2+(\frac{3}{2})^2} \\
&= \sqrt{16+\frac{9}{4}} \\
&= \frac{\sqrt{73}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the magnitude of $q+r$ is $\frac{\sqrt{73}}{2}$. Consequently, the unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}
u &= \frac{1}{|q+r|}\cdot (q+r) \\
&= \frac{2 \sqrt{73}}{73}(q+r)
\end{aligned}
$$
